activations.domainDescription: Central hub for metabolic homeostasis integrating leptin, insulin, ghrelin, and glucose signals
activations.domainFunction: Coordinates appetite, satiety, thermogenesis, and autonomic metabolic regulation via arcuate, ventromedial, and lateral hypothalamic nuclei
activations.whyThisNode: The hypothalamus is the master integrator of peripheral metabolic signals — leptin/insulin resistance here is the upstream driver of obesity, diabetes, and neuroendocrine dysfunction

treatments.label: GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy
treatments.description: Semaglutide/tirzepatide restores hypothalamic satiety signaling and reduces appetite drive via GLP-1R activation in arcuate nucleus

treatments.label: Time-restricted eating protocol
treatments.description: Aligning food intake with circadian hypothalamic rhythms restores insulin sensitivity cycling and leptin signaling fidelity

activations.domainDescription: Master endocrine gland transducing hypothalamic signals into peripheral hormone cascades
activations.domainFunction: Secretes ACTH, TSH, GH, LH/FSH, and prolactin in response to hypothalamic releasing factors, governing adrenal, thyroid, gonadal, and growth axes
activations.whyThisNode: The pituitary is the signal transducer between central neural commands and peripheral endocrine organs — its dysfunction cascades across every metabolic axis

treatments.label: Targeted hormone replacement
treatments.description: Axis-specific replacement (levothyroxine, hydrocortisone, GH) restores downstream signaling cascades disrupted by pituitary dysfunction

treatments.label: Dynamic pituitary function testing
treatments.description: ACTH stimulation, TRH stimulation, and insulin tolerance testing to map residual pituitary reserve across all axes

activations.domainDescription: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis linking stress responses to metabolic regulation
activations.domainFunction: Regulates cortisol output that modulates hepatic gluconeogenesis, visceral adiposity, insulin resistance, and hippocampal vulnerability
activations.whyThisNode: Chronic HPA dysregulation is the central mediator between psychological stress and metabolic disease — cortisol excess drives insulin resistance, visceral fat accumulation, and hippocampal atrophy

treatments.label: Cortisol synthesis inhibitors
treatments.description: Osilodrostat or ketoconazole blocks adrenal steroidogenesis to normalize cortisol in Cushing's, protecting hippocampus and restoring insulin sensitivity

treatments.label: Stress reduction and HPA normalization
treatments.description: Mindfulness-based stress reduction attenuates cortisol output, reducing cortisol-mediated insulin resistance and visceral adipogenesis

crossDomainAffinities.role: Attentional Control — Feedback & Validation — Tertiary Node

activations.domainDescription: Adrenal cortex production of cortisol, aldosterone, and androgens
activations.domainFunction: Synthesizes glucocorticoids for metabolic regulation, mineralocorticoids for electrolyte balance, and androgens as sex hormone precursors
activations.whyThisNode: The adrenal gland is the effector organ for both cortisol excess (Cushing's) and deficiency (Addison's) — its output directly determines metabolic substrate availability and vascular tone

treatments.label: Physiologic glucocorticoid replacement
treatments.description: Modified-release hydrocortisone mimics circadian cortisol rhythm, restoring metabolic substrate regulation in adrenal insufficiency

treatments.label: Adrenal crisis prevention education
treatments.description: Structured self-management training for stress dosing prevents life-threatening adrenal crisis during metabolic demands

activations.domainDescription: Prefrontal executive function governing dietary decisions, treatment adherence, and impulse regulation
activations.domainFunction: Provides top-down inhibitory control over hedonic eating, supports working memory for glycemic management, and sustains attention for self-care behaviors
activations.whyThisNode: Prefrontal cortex is the first cortical casualty of metabolic disease — cerebral glucose hypometabolism, insulin resistance, and thyroid deficiency all impair executive function, creating a vicious cycle of poor self-management

treatments.label: Cognitive rehabilitation during metabolic optimization
treatments.description: Structured executive function training concurrent with metabolic correction addresses residual prefrontal deficits from chronic hyperglycemia or thyroid deficiency

treatments.label: Diabetes self-management education
treatments.description: Structured behavioral program leveraging prefrontal executive capacity to improve glycemic control and reduce cognitive burden of disease management

activations.domainDescription: Hippocampal plasticity and memory function as targets of metabolic injury
activations.domainFunction: Hippocampal insulin receptors regulate synaptic plasticity and neurogenesis — chronic hyperglycemia, cortisol excess, and thyroid deficiency each independently drive hippocampal atrophy
activations.whyThisNode: The hippocampus is exquisitely sensitive to metabolic insult — it contains the highest density of insulin receptors, glucocorticoid receptors, and thyroid hormone receptors in the brain, making it the convergence point for metabolic neurodegeneration

treatments.label: Aerobic exercise for hippocampal neurogenesis
treatments.description: Structured aerobic exercise upregulates hippocampal BDNF, improves insulin sensitivity, and reverses diabetes-associated hippocampal atrophy

treatments.label: Mediterranean dietary pattern
treatments.description: Anti-inflammatory polyphenols and omega-3 fatty acids enhance cerebrovascular function and reduce AGE-mediated hippocampal damage

activations.domainDescription: Nucleus accumbens hedonic food reward processing and dopaminergic appetite drive
activations.domainFunction: Integrates dopaminergic reward signals with metabolic state to drive food-seeking behavior — hyperinsulinemia and leptin resistance amplify hedonic eating via mesolimbic sensitization
activations.whyThisNode: The nucleus accumbens is where metabolic disease hijacks reward circuitry — insulin resistance increases food cue responsivity, and GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce appetite partly by dampening NAcc activation to food cues

treatments.label: GLP-1RA reward circuit modulation
treatments.description: Semaglutide reduces nucleus accumbens food cue reactivity via central GLP-1 receptors, decoupling hedonic drive from metabolic hunger

treatments.label: CBT for emotional and hedonic eating
treatments.description: Cognitive-behavioral therapy addresses maladaptive reward-seeking eating patterns by strengthening prefrontal inhibitory control over NAcc-driven cravings

activations.domainDescription: Ventral tegmental area dopamine output modulated by peripheral metabolic hormones
activations.domainFunction: Insulin and leptin receptors on VTA dopamine neurons modulate reward valuation of food — metabolic hormone resistance shifts dopaminergic tone toward compulsive eating
activations.whyThisNode: VTA dopamine neurons express insulin and leptin receptors — metabolic hormone resistance directly alters reward circuit gain, transforming normal appetite into pathological food-seeking in obesity and metabolic syndrome

treatments.label: Naltrexone/bupropion combination
treatments.description: Opioid antagonism plus norepinephrine/dopamine reuptake inhibition normalizes VTA reward signaling to reduce compulsive food intake

treatments.label: Structured physical activity program
treatments.description: Regular exercise normalizes VTA dopamine signaling and restores insulin sensitivity in mesolimbic reward circuits

activations.domainDescription: Anterior insular cortex processing visceral metabolic signals including glucose status, gut distension, and autonomic state
activations.domainFunction: Integrates interoceptive signals from peripheral metabolic sensors into conscious awareness of hunger, satiety, and metabolic distress — dysregulated in diabetes and obesity
activations.whyThisNode: The anterior insula is the cortical gateway for visceral metabolic signals — disrupted interoception in diabetes impairs glucose sensing, while insular hyperactivation in obesity amplifies food cue responsivity

treatments.label: Interoceptive awareness training
treatments.description: Mindful eating and body scan practices recalibrate insular interoceptive processing to improve hunger-satiety discrimination

treatments.label: Continuous glucose monitoring biofeedback
treatments.description: Real-time CGM data provides external interoceptive signal to compensate for disrupted insular glucose sensing in diabetes

activations.domainDescription: Bidirectional communication between gut microbiome and brain affecting metabolic regulation
activations.domainFunction: Gut microbiota produce SCFAs, modulate incretin secretion, regulate intestinal permeability, and influence central appetite circuits via vagal afferents and humoral signaling
activations.whyThisNode: The gut-brain axis is the second metabolic brain — microbiome dysbiosis in metabolic syndrome drives endotoxemia, neuroinflammation, and disrupted incretin signaling that worsen insulin resistance and central appetite dysregulation

treatments.label: Prebiotic fiber supplementation
treatments.description: Prebiotic fibers increase Akkermansia and Bifidobacteria populations, improving gut barrier integrity and GLP-1 secretion to restore metabolic signaling

treatments.label: Mediterranean dietary pattern for microbiome restoration
treatments.description: Plant-rich Mediterranean diet increases microbial diversity, SCFA production, and reduces LPS translocation driving neuroinflammation

crossDomainAffinities.role: Screen Reader Compatibility Human Capital & Development

activations.domainDescription: Intrinsic gut nervous system coordinating digestion and metabolic hormone release
activations.domainFunction: The enteric nervous system independently regulates GI motility, incretin hormone secretion, and nutrient absorption, relaying metabolic information centrally via vagal and spinal afferents
activations.whyThisNode: The ENS contains more neurons than the spinal cord and directly controls incretin release (GLP-1, GIP) that is the target of the most effective obesity and diabetes therapeutics — enteric dysfunction disrupts the metabolic signaling chain at its source

treatments.label: Prokinetic and incretin optimization
treatments.description: GLP-1 receptor agonists enhance enteric incretin signaling, improving glucose-dependent insulin secretion and gastric emptying regulation

treatments.label: Probiotic multi-strain therapy
treatments.description: Targeted probiotic strains restore enteric nervous system signaling fidelity and reduce gut-mediated metabolic inflammation

activations.domainDescription: Ventral vagal pathways conveying gut nutrient and metabolic status to brainstem and hypothalamus
activations.domainFunction: Vagal afferents from hepatoportal glucose sensors, intestinal nutrient detectors, and adipose tissue relay real-time metabolic state to NTS and hypothalamus for energy homeostasis
activations.whyThisNode: The vagus nerve is the primary information highway between peripheral metabolism and the brain — vagal afferent signaling of nutrient status is critical for meal termination, and bariatric surgery works partly by altering vagal metabolic signaling

treatments.label: Vagal nerve stimulation for appetite modulation
treatments.description: Transcutaneous auricular vagal nerve stimulation modulates vagal metabolic afferents to reduce appetite and improve glucose regulation

treatments.label: Post-bariatric vagal remodeling support
treatments.description: Structured eating protocols after bariatric surgery optimize altered vagal satiety signaling for sustained metabolic benefit

activations.domainDescription: Nucleus tractus solitarius integrating vagal metabolic afferents with autonomic outflow
activations.domainFunction: NTS receives vagal afferents carrying hepatoportal glucose, gut peptide, and cardiovascular information, integrating these into autonomic metabolic regulation and relaying to hypothalamus
activations.whyThisNode: The NTS is the first central relay for peripheral metabolic signals — it integrates gut-derived GLP-1, CCK, and glucose information before forwarding to hypothalamus, making it a critical node in the metabolic sensing chain

treatments.label: Slow-paced eating for NTS satiety signaling
treatments.description: Extending meal duration allows vagal-NTS satiety signaling to reach threshold before caloric overconsumption, improving portion calibration

treatments.label: GLP-1RA brainstem activation
treatments.description: GLP-1 receptor agonists activate NTS neurons directly via area postrema access, reducing appetite through brainstem satiety circuits

activations.domainDescription: Sympathetic nervous system regulation of metabolic rate, lipolysis, and thermogenesis
activations.domainFunction: Sympathetic outflow drives adipose tissue lipolysis, hepatic glucose output, and adaptive thermogenesis — chronic sympathetic overactivation in metabolic syndrome worsens insulin resistance and hypertension
activations.whyThisNode: Sympathetic overdrive is both a consequence and driver of metabolic syndrome — catecholamine excess worsens insulin resistance, promotes visceral adiposity, and increases cardiovascular risk through the metabolic-autonomic feedback loop

treatments.label: Sympatholytic therapy for metabolic hypertension
treatments.description: Alpha/beta-adrenergic blockade in pheochromocytoma and metabolic syndrome reduces sympathetic-driven insulin resistance and cardiovascular risk

treatments.label: Heart rate variability biofeedback
treatments.description: HRV training reduces sympathetic dominance, improving autonomic balance to lower metabolic syndrome cardiovascular risk

activations.domainDescription: BDNF-mediated neuroplasticity as a target of metabolic injury and recovery
activations.domainFunction: BDNF expression is suppressed by hyperglycemia, cortisol excess, and thyroid deficiency while being upregulated by exercise, insulin sensitizers, and metabolic correction — it is the molecular bridge between metabolic health and brain plasticity
activations.whyThisNode: BDNF is the convergence point for metabolic neuroprotection — every major metabolic insult (diabetes, cortisol excess, thyroid deficiency) suppresses BDNF, and every effective intervention (exercise, metformin, thyroid replacement) restores it

treatments.label: Exercise-induced BDNF upregulation
treatments.description: Moderate-to-vigorous aerobic exercise increases circulating BDNF 2-3x, promoting hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity despite metabolic disease

treatments.label: Metabolic optimization for BDNF restoration
treatments.description: Metformin AMPK activation and thyroid hormone replacement both independently restore BDNF expression suppressed by metabolic dysfunction

activations.domainDescription: Raphe nuclei serotonin synthesis dependent on thyroid hormone and metabolic cofactors
activations.domainFunction: T3 is a direct cofactor for tryptophan hydroxylase-2 expression — thyroid deficiency reduces serotonin synthesis, while gut-derived serotonin from enterochromaffin cells modulates appetite and GI motility
activations.whyThisNode: The raphe nuclei link endocrine and mood dysfunction — hypothyroidism-induced serotonin deficiency explains the high comorbidity of depression with thyroid disease, and 95% of body serotonin is gut-derived, linking metabolic and affective pathways

treatments.label: Thyroid hormone restoration of serotonergic tone
treatments.description: Levothyroxine restores T3-dependent tryptophan hydroxylase-2 expression, normalizing raphe serotonin synthesis in hypothyroidism

treatments.label: Tryptophan-adequate nutritional support
treatments.description: Ensuring dietary tryptophan sufficiency supports serotonin synthesis when thyroid optimization restores enzymatic capacity

activations.domainDescription: Ventromedial prefrontal cortex integrating emotional processing with metabolic decision-making
activations.domainFunction: vmPFC atrophy from cortisol excess impairs emotional regulation and value-based dietary decision-making — it is the convergence point for mood disorders comorbid with metabolic disease
activations.whyThisNode: The vmPFC integrates emotional valence with metabolic choices — cortisol-induced vmPFC atrophy in Cushing's syndrome explains the 50-80% depression comorbidity, and vmPFC dysfunction drives emotional eating in obesity

treatments.label: CBT for metabolic comorbid depression
treatments.description: Cognitive-behavioral therapy addresses cortisol-amplified cognitive distortions and emotional dysregulation in metabolic disease comorbid depression

treatments.label: Cortisol normalization for vmPFC recovery
treatments.description: Surgical or pharmacological cortisol normalization in Cushing's allows partial vmPFC volume recovery over 12-24 months

activations.domainDescription: Orbitofrontal cortex encoding hedonic food value and reward prediction
activations.domainFunction: OFC assigns subjective value to food stimuli and integrates taste, smell, and texture into reward representations — hyperactivation in obesity overvalues calorie-dense foods relative to metabolic need
activations.whyThisNode: The OFC is the hedonic evaluator that assigns disproportionate reward value to calorie-dense foods in obesity — its hyperactivation explains why food choices resist rational dietary planning despite intact prefrontal knowledge

treatments.label: Mindful eating revaluation training
treatments.description: Structured mindful eating practices reduce OFC hypervaluation of calorie-dense foods by increasing conscious awareness of reward-satiety mismatch

treatments.label: GLP-1RA food reward dampening
treatments.description: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce OFC response to food cues, normalizing reward valuation to align with metabolic need rather than hedonic drive

activations.domainDescription: Basolateral amygdala threat processing amplified by metabolic hormonal dysregulation
activations.domainFunction: Cortisol excess, hyperandrogenism, and hypoglycemia each independently amplify BLA threat reactivity — driving anxiety comorbidity across metabolic and endocrine disorders
activations.whyThisNode: The BLA is hyperactivated across metabolic disorders — cortisol excess in Cushing's, androgen excess in PCOS, and catecholamine surges in hypoglycemia all converge on amygdala threat circuits, explaining the 2-3x elevated anxiety prevalence

treatments.label: Hormonal normalization of amygdala reactivity
treatments.description: Cortisol normalization in Cushing's and androgen reduction in PCOS reduce BLA hyperactivation, alleviating metabolic-driven anxiety

treatments.label: Exposure-based anxiety management
treatments.description: Graduated exposure therapy for hypoglycemia fear and metabolic-condition-related anxiety retrains amygdala threat calibration

activations.domainDescription: Dorsal anterior cingulate cortex monitoring conflicts between metabolic drives and behavioral goals
activations.domainFunction: dACC detects conflicts between appetite drives and dietary goals, signaling the need for executive intervention — its activation reflects the cognitive effort of metabolic self-management
activations.whyThisNode: The dACC is continuously engaged in metabolic disease self-management — monitoring conflicts between food cravings and glycemic targets, mediating the cognitive burden of chronic disease management that drives diabetes distress

treatments.label: Acceptance and commitment therapy for metabolic management
treatments.description: ACT reduces dACC hyperactivation from metabolic self-management burden by changing relationship to dietary urges rather than suppressing them

treatments.label: Decision fatigue reduction protocols
treatments.description: Meal planning and structured dietary routines reduce dACC conflict-monitoring demands, freeing executive resources for other self-management tasks

activations.domainDescription: Locus coeruleus norepinephrine output modulated by thyroid hormone and metabolic state
activations.domainFunction: LC noradrenergic tone is reduced in hypothyroidism and amplified during hypoglycemia and pheochromocytoma — driving fatigue or hyperarousal depending on metabolic context
activations.whyThisNode: The locus coeruleus translates metabolic state into arousal level — thyroid hormone deficiency reduces LC output causing fatigue, while hypoglycemia triggers LC noradrenergic storms causing panic-like autonomic activation

treatments.label: Thyroid hormone restoration of noradrenergic tone
treatments.description: Levothyroxine normalizes LC norepinephrine output, improving arousal, attention, and fatigue in hypothyroidism

treatments.label: Graded activity for noradrenergic calibration
treatments.description: Progressive exercise increases LC tonic firing and noradrenergic tone without metabolic destabilization in endocrine fatigue states

activations.domainDescription: Cerebellar function affected by thyroid deficiency and mitochondrial energy failure
activations.domainFunction: Cerebellar Purkinje cells are exquisitely dependent on thyroid hormone for maturation and on oxidative phosphorylation for sustained firing — hypothyroidism and mitochondrial disease cause cerebellar ataxia
activations.whyThisNode: The cerebellum is a sentinel for metabolic disease — Purkinje cell dysfunction in severe hypothyroidism causes ataxia, while cerebellar energy demands make it vulnerable to mitochondrial dysfunction and hypoglycemia

treatments.label: Thyroid replacement for cerebellar recovery
treatments.description: Adequate levothyroxine dosing restores thyroid-dependent cerebellar Purkinje cell function, improving coordination and balance

treatments.label: Balance and coordination rehabilitation
treatments.description: Vestibular and cerebellar rehabilitation exercises accelerate functional recovery during thyroid hormone optimization

activations.domainDescription: Thalamic relay function disrupted by glycemic excursions and metabolic encephalopathy
activations.domainFunction: Thalamocortical gating is disrupted during acute glycemic excursions and metabolic encephalopathy — thalamic relay integrity is essential for sensory processing and cortical arousal that depend on stable glucose supply
activations.whyThisNode: The thalamus is the cortical gatekeeper that fails during metabolic crisis — acute hypoglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis, and hepatic encephalopathy all disrupt thalamocortical relay, producing the confusion and altered consciousness of metabolic emergencies

treatments.label: Glycemic stabilization for thalamocortical integrity
treatments.description: Tight glycemic control with CGM-guided insulin management prevents glycemic excursions that disrupt thalamocortical relay function

treatments.label: Arousal and attention monitoring during metabolic correction
treatments.description: Serial neurological assessment during metabolic correction tracks thalamocortical recovery as a proxy for central metabolic normalization

activations.domainDescription: Microbiome-driven endotoxemia and adipose-derived cytokine signaling causing central neuroinflammation
activations.domainFunction: Gut dysbiosis increases LPS translocation across compromised intestinal barrier, while visceral adipose tissue secretes TNF-alpha and IL-6 that cross the BBB, activating microglia and driving neuroinflammation that worsens insulin resistance in hippocampus and hypothalamus
activations.whyThisNode: Metabolic inflammation is the unifying pathology linking obesity, insulin resistance, and neurodegeneration — microbiome-derived endotoxemia and adipokine signaling create a chronic low-grade neuroinflammatory state that accelerates brain aging in metabolic disease

treatments.label: Targeted microbiome restoration
treatments.description: High-fiber Mediterranean diet combined with fermented foods increases microbial diversity and SCFA production to restore metabolic signaling

treatments.label: Metformin microbiome modulation
treatments.description: Metformin's metabolic benefits are partially mediated through microbiome changes including increased Akkermansia muciniphila abundance

issues.label: Type 2 Diabetes
issues.summary: Chronic hyperglycemia and insulin resistance drive cerebral glucose hypometabolism, hippocampal atrophy, and accelerated cognitive decline via hypothalamic insulin signaling disruption and HPA axis dysregulation

_authored.detail: Hypothalamic insulin receptor desensitization disrupts appetite-satiety signaling and autonomic glucose regulation via arcuate nucleus leptin/insulin resistance
Hippocampal atrophy from chronic hyperglycemia and advanced glycation end-product accumulation impairs episodic memory and spatial navigation
Reduced cerebral glucose utilization in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex impairs executive function, working memory, and treatment adherence
Insular cortex interoceptive processing disrupted — impaired visceral glucose sensing leads to poor glycemic awareness
Chronic HPA axis activation with elevated cortisol accelerates hippocampal neurodegeneration and compounds insulin resistance
Hyperglycemia suppresses BDNF expression, impairing synaptic plasticity and neuronal survival in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex
Gut microbiome dysbiosis alters SCFA production and incretin signaling, driving endotoxemia that worsens central and peripheral insulin resistance

issues.label: Hypothyroidism
issues.summary: Thyroid hormone deficiency reduces cerebral metabolic rate, impairs myelination and synaptic plasticity, and slows serotonin/norepinephrine synthesis critical for hippocampal neurogenesis and prefrontal function

circuits.detail: pituitary — endocrine output (HPA/HPG axis) — hormonal insufficiency

_authored.detail: Prefrontal hypometabolism causes executive dysfunction, poor concentration, and psychomotor slowing from reduced T3-dependent neuronal energy production
Impaired hippocampal neurogenesis and LTP from T3-dependent BDNF expression reduction causes memory consolidation deficits
Serotonin synthesis reduced because T3 is a direct cofactor for tryptophan hydroxylase-2 expression in raphe nuclei
Noradrenergic output reduced contributing to characteristic fatigue, cognitive slowing, and cold intolerance of hypothyroidism
Hypothalamic TRH hypersecretion in primary hypothyroidism from loss of T3/T4 negative feedback
Cerebellar Purkinje cell dysfunction in severe hypothyroidism causes ataxia, dysmetria, and balance impairment

issues.label: Metabolic Syndrome
issues.summary: Cluster of insulin resistance, visceral adiposity, dyslipidemia, and hypertension driven by hypothalamic energy sensing failure, sympathetic overdrive, and chronic low-grade neuroinflammation

_authored.detail: Hypothalamic leptin and insulin receptor resistance disrupts energy homeostasis signaling, maintaining elevated body weight set-point despite caloric excess
Chronic sympathetic overdrive drives hypertension, promotes lipolysis dysregulation, and worsens insulin resistance through catecholamine excess
Elevated cortisol promotes visceral adipogenesis, hepatic gluconeogenesis, and central insulin resistance in a self-amplifying metabolic loop
Increased gut permeability and metabolic endotoxemia drive systemic and neuroinflammation that worsen insulin resistance across all tissues
Prefrontal hypometabolism proportional to insulin resistance severity impairs executive dietary control and self-management
Nucleus accumbens hyperresponsive to food cues from dopaminergic reward dysregulation driven by hyperinsulinemia
Insular cortex amplifies visceral metabolic distress signals, contributing to somatic complaints and interoceptive confusion

issues.label: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
issues.summary: Neuroendocrine disorder with hypothalamic GnRH pulse frequency acceleration, hyperandrogenism, and insulin resistance affecting prefrontal function, reward circuits, and mood regulation

circuits.detail: pituitary — endocrine output (HPA/HPG axis) — hormonal overdrive

_authored.detail: Accelerated GnRH pulse frequency drives LH hypersecretion and ovarian/adrenal androgen excess as the primary neuroendocrine defect
Insulin resistance-mediated prefrontal hypometabolism impairs executive function and contributes to cognitive complaints
Reward processing altered by hyperinsulinemia with elevated food cravings and emotional eating patterns
Adrenal androgen excess with HPA axis hyperactivation amplifies hyperandrogenism beyond ovarian contribution
Anxiety prevalence 3x higher than controls from combined androgen and insulin effects on amygdala threat circuits
Gut microbiome dysbiosis correlates with androgen levels and may amplify metabolic and hormonal dysregulation

issues.label: Cushing's Syndrome
issues.summary: Chronic cortisol excess is profoundly neurotoxic causing hippocampal volume loss up to 25%, prefrontal atrophy, and amygdala hyperactivation with depression in 50-80% of patients

circuits.detail: pituitary — endocrine output (HPA/HPG axis) — hormonal overdrive

_authored.detail: Hippocampal atrophy from glucocorticoid neurotoxicity causes up to 25% volume loss with severe declarative memory impairment
Autonomous cortisol overproduction disrupts negative feedback, creating sustained glucocorticoid excess throughout the brain
Prefrontal cortex thinning causes executive dysfunction, poor working memory, and impaired cognitive flexibility
Amygdala hyperactivation drives anxiety, emotional lability, and irritability through cortisol-sensitized threat circuits
Ventromedial PFC atrophy impairs emotional regulation, contributing to the 50-80% depression prevalence in active Cushing's
Cortisol directly suppresses BDNF gene expression, reducing hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity

issues.label: Adrenal Insufficiency
issues.summary: Cortisol and aldosterone deficiency impairs prefrontal executive function, hippocampal memory, and energy homeostasis with fatigue and cognitive complaints persisting despite replacement therapy

circuits.detail: pituitary — endocrine output (HPA/HPG axis) — hormonal insufficiency

_authored.detail: Cortisol deficiency causes loss of permissive glucocorticoid signaling throughout the brain, impairing metabolic substrate availability for neurons
Executive function and concentration impaired even with cortisol replacement, suggesting non-physiologic replacement kinetics
Memory impairment from inadequate mineralocorticoid receptor activation despite glucocorticoid replacement
CRH hypersecretion from loss of cortisol negative feedback drives fatigue and mood symptoms independent of cortisol levels
Adrenergic insufficiency with crisis risk from sympathetic dysregulation during metabolic stress
Fatigue perception amplified through insular interoceptive processing, contributing to persistent quality-of-life impairment

issues.label: Neurometabolic Obesity
issues.summary: Hypothalamic leptin/insulin resistance, reward circuit hijacking, and prefrontal inhibitory failure drive pathological weight gain while neuroinflammation from adipose tissue crosses the BBB to impair hippocampal plasticity

_authored.detail: Leptin and insulin resistance in arcuate nucleus disrupts satiety signaling, maintaining elevated body weight set-point
Nucleus accumbens hyperresponsive to food cues with dopaminergic reward circuit sensitization driving compulsive eating
Prefrontal inhibitory control impaired — reduced capacity to override hedonic eating despite intact dietary knowledge
Insular cortex hyperresponsive to food taste and smell cues, amplifying anticipated reward from calorie-dense foods
Gut dysbiosis increases LPS translocation, driving central neuroinflammation that impairs hippocampal and hypothalamic function
Hippocampal atrophy from adipose-derived neuroinflammation impairs meal-related memory encoding and satiety learning
Orbitofrontal cortex hypervalues food reward, assigning disproportionate hedonic weight to calorie-dense stimuli

issues.label: Insulin Resistance
issues.summary: Central insulin resistance impairs hypothalamic energy sensing, prefrontal executive function, and hippocampal plasticity before overt diabetes develops, representing the earliest neurocognitive stage of metabolic disease

_authored.detail: Hypothalamic insulin and leptin receptor resistance disrupts energy homeostasis signaling before peripheral glucose rises
Hippocampal insulin resistance reduces long-term potentiation and spatial memory performance in pre-diabetic state
Prefrontal hypometabolism proportional to insulin resistance severity detectable before diabetes diagnosis
Nucleus accumbens hyperresponsive to food cues from dopaminergic reward dysregulation amplified by hyperinsulinemia
Elevated cortisol worsens visceral adiposity and hepatic insulin resistance in a bidirectional metabolic-stress amplification loop
Gut permeability and endotoxemia drive systemic and neuroinflammation that precedes and accelerates progression to overt diabetes
